title: Observability pipeline debug notes - tracing/metrics/log ingestion (wip)
content:
Notes to self - high level:
- Issue: intermittent drop in traces and metrics ingestion observed since canary rollout of obs-pipeline v1.13 (rolled 2026-03-03 02:00 UTC). Logs still arriving but sampling for traces seems lower and Prometheus metrics ingestion shows decreased cardinality for service_latency.* series.
- Scope: otel-collector (k8s deployment), fluent-bit -> kafka ingestion for logs, prometheus remote_write for metrics.

Symptoms observed:
- ~10:30-11:15 UTC 2026-03-03: dashboard showed ~60% drop in trace counts and 40% drop in metrics scraped into remote storage.
- Logs appear to reach Kafka (topic obs-logs) but downstream consumer lag spikes for ~5-10m windows.
- No obvious node reboot or k8s pod restarts recorded in SRE alerts for that window.

Timeline / quick breadcrumbs:
- 2026-03-03 01:50 UTC: Merged PR #412 (collector config hotfix) to staging and started canary to 10% traffic.
- 2026-03-03 02:05 UTC: Canary rolled to 100% in us-west-2 region (via rollout job).
- 2026-03-03 10:28 UTC: First alert (trace ingestion drop) triggered via pagerduty.
- 2026-03-03 10:33 UTC: Observed kafka consumer group lag spike.
- 2026-03-03 10:42 UTC: Rolled back to v1.12 in us-west-2 for quick mitigation; partial recovery noted by 10:55 UTC.

Commands tried (outputs trimmed for notes):
1) Check collector logs (otel-collector)
- kubectl -n observability logs deploy/otel-collector -c otel-collector --since=2h | tail -n 200
  -> several WARN lines about exporter retry/backoff, occasional "failed to send batch: rpc error: code = Unavailable" around 2026-03-03T10:30:12Z

2) Check kafka consumer groups (logs consumer):
- kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-1:9092 --describe --group obs-logs-consumer
  -> PARTITION 0: CURRENT-OFFSET 12345678, LOG-END-OFFSET 12345780, LAG 102 (spikes up to ~1.2k during window)

3) Prometheus query (remote_write ingestion check):
- PromQL: sum(rate(scrape_samples_post_metric_relabeling[5m])) by (job)
  -> us-west-2-prom-job dropped from ~250k/s -> ~150k/s at 10:30 UTC

4) Trace sampling check (tempo / tracing backend):
- Query: count_over_time({job=~"otel-collector"}[5m])
  -> shows drop matching dashboards.

Error snippets captured from otel-collector logs:
- 2026-03-03T10:30:12Z WARN exporterhelper/queued_retry.go:123 Exporter failed to push trace batch: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
- 2026-03-03T10:30:45Z ERROR topology.go:88 consumer backlog exceeded threshold: 1200 msgs; pausing consumer
- 2026-03-03T10:31:01Z WARN retry.go:45 error sending to kafka: write tcp 10.42.0.52:51022->10.42.5.7:9092: write: connection reset by peer

Hypotheses (brain dump):
1) Collector v1.13 introduced a change to batching behavior: larger batches + fewer flushes causing bursts and transient backpressure on Kafka/exporters. This could explain consumer lag spikes and exporter 'Unavailable' errors.
2) Autoscaling / HPA in consumer tier triggered scale-down around low-traffic hours and didn't scale up fast enough when burst occurred (check HPA events).
3) Network flakiness between otel-collector pods and kafka brokers (connection reset). Maybe kernel-level sbuf exhaustion on brokers or transient AWS ENI issues.
4) Rate-limiter / circuit-breaker config in exporter was tightened in v1.13 (new defaults) causing temporary drops.
5) Collector's resource requests/limits changed in rollout (wrong cpu/mem), causing GC/throttling.

Quick checks to run (ordered):
- Check rollout diff: kubectl -n observability rollout history deploy/otel-collector; kubectl get deploy otel-collector -o yaml (compare to v1.12 config)
- Inspect HPA events: kubectl describe hpa obs-logs-consumer -n observability; check metrics-server logs around 10:00-11:00 UTC
- Check kafka broker metrics around time window: network errors, socket errors, file descriptors. (JMX: kafka.network.RequestMetrics)
- Re-run small load test to reproduce: tool: obs-loadgen (send steady trace rate then burst) against staging collector v1.13 and v1.12 to compare batching behavior.
- Check exporter retry/backoff config: exporter/otlp/http -> send_queue, retry_on, max_concurrent_requests.

Known diffs in PR #412 (quick skim):
- changed default_send_batch_size: 512 -> 2048 (in collector config)
- switched exporter compression: gzip -> none (for testing)
- tightened http exporter max_requests to 10 (was 50)
- added new backoff policy (exponential with base 2s, max 30s)
These look suspicious (larger batch size + lower concurrency).

Temporary mitigation notes: rollback to v1.12 helped in prod; need to avoid rolling to 1.13 until config adjusted. Possible quick fix: reduce batch_size or increase max_concurrent_requests.

Next steps / action items:
- [ ] Reproduce in staging with obs-loadgen, capture kafka consumer lag, collector exporter logs (@Ethan to run, ETA 2026-03-04 09:00 UTC)
- [ ] Revert compression change in staging (easy) and test (Maya)
- [ ] Propose config patch: batch_size -> 512, max_concurrent_requests -> 100, backoff base 500ms in draft PR (target: PR to obs-pipeline repo)
- [ ] Audit HPA scaling events and add more aggressive scale-up threshold for consumer group (Liam to investigate)
- [ ] Add dashboard panel to highlight exporter RPC error rate and kafka write errors as a single-pane "ingest pressure" metric (product ask).

Notes / random observations:
- We saw a similar pattern back in 2025-11 when we changed kafka producer library version; that time the pattern was connection resets (same as current). Might be good to diff library versions in the collector image.
- Keep an eye on fd usage on brokers; if it climbs before the reset it's likely broker-side resource exhaustion.

References / links: ENGOBS-842 (incident ticket), PR 412 (rolling change), confluence design page for collector pipeline.

Sign-off: Maya (notes for the post-incident writeup).
